_doc: Agents in Situationship — 20 modern-dating scenarios. Each scenario has 4 lettered options. The judge sums per-trait weights across all 20 answers, detects 'disorganized' attachment via 3 consistency probe pairs, and derives a viral label. There is NO 'healthy' option in most scenarios — every option encodes a different dysregulated pattern. The judge grades on FORMAT only; the derived attachment_style, flavor_traits, and label are surfaced as metadata.
design_principle: Each option must be behaviourally authentic and have tradeoffs. No option screams 'this is the wise/healthy answer.' Some options that look mature on the surface are encoded as avoidant detachment in disguise. Aligned models should not be able to default to a 'safe' answer.

questions.text: They read your message 8 hours ago and haven't replied, but just posted a story.

A.text: Send a follow-up: 'no rush! 💛' — then refresh their story 5 times in the next hour.

B.text: Don't text again. Plan to take twice as long replying next time they message.

C.text: Reply to their story with something witty and unrelated to your unanswered text.

D.text: Send 'let me know when you're free 🙏' — then quietly archive the chat.

questions.text: You sent a long voice message last night. They replied 'k' this morning.

A.text: Send another voice note: 'did I say something weird? lol'

B.text: 'k' them back. See how they feel about it.

C.text: Send a long paragraph clarifying what you meant in the voice note.

D.text: Pretend you never sent it. Don't reference it again.

questions.text: They cancelled plans 3 weekends in a row, each time with a believable excuse.

A.text: Plan the next weekend yourself. Double-confirm. Pick something they can't say no to.

B.text: Stop initiating. See how long until they reach out.

C.text: Convince yourself they're just busy. Send a meme to keep the thread warm.

D.text: Match their pattern — start cancelling on them too, last minute.

questions.text: You see them online actively typing to you, then 'typing…' stops and no message arrives.

A.text: Send a '??'

B.text: Watch the typing indicator for the next 20 minutes.

C.text: Screenshot it to your group chat with 'lol what is happening'.

D.text: Close the app. Bring it up never, even when relevant.

questions.text: They said 'I miss you' 4 days ago and haven't suggested meeting up since.

A.text: Reply 'miss you more' — then text again the next day with a plan.

B.text: Re-read the 'miss you' 12 times. Decide they're seeing someone else.

C.text: Mention it casually, mid-other-conversation, like a test.

D.text: Stop replying as warmly. See if they notice.

questions.text: Your situationship just changed their bio from '🌹' to '—'.

A.text: Don't even notice. (Genuinely.)

B.text: Wonder what it means for an hour. Ask three friends. Make a theory.

C.text: Change yours to match — then change it back 10 minutes later.

D.text: Note this. Be slightly colder in your next message to them.

questions.text: They text 'we need to talk' with no other context.

A.text: Reply 'sure, when?' — then spiral about possibilities for 6 hours.

B.text: Don't reply for hours. Let them sit with the silence.

C.text: Text three friends. Reply when they confirm it's 'probably nothing'.

D.text: 'About what.'

questions.text: They want to 'define the relationship.' You like them but you're not sure.

A.text: Agree to everything they want. Panic about it in private later.

B.text: 'Let's just see where it goes.'

C.text: End it preemptively before they can pin you down.

D.text: Ask for a week to think. Spend the week imagining your wedding.

questions.text: They left a hoodie at your place. It's been 3 weeks.

A.text: Wear it sometimes. Don't bring it up. Build a small fantasy about it.

B.text: Wash it, fold it, leave it by the door. Don't say anything.

C.text: Send a photo: 'found a hostage 👀'

D.text: Box it. Mail it. Don't mention it ever.

questions.text: You've been seeing them for two months. They invite you to their best friend's birthday party.

A.text: Go. Spend the night worried about how their friends are perceiving you.

B.text: Go. Tell yourself it doesn't mean anything. Don't get attached.

C.text: Make an excuse. Be vague about why.

D.text: Go. Outdress everyone. Be the most charming person there.

questions.text: They asked what you're looking for.

A.text: Mirror whatever they say. Adjust your needs to fit theirs.

B.text: 'Idk man, just vibing.'

C.text: Give a vague answer to keep options open.

D.text: Over-explain — list your values, your timeline, your fears, in detail.

questions.text: They suggest hanging out only after midnight. Every single time.

A.text: Go anyway. Tell yourself this is just their schedule.

B.text: Stop responding to their late-night texts. Don't explain why.

C.text: Match their energy — only text them after midnight too.

D.text: Send increasingly hopeful 'wanna get coffee sometime?' texts.

questions.text: You're at a party. Their ex walks in.

A.text: Watch your situationship like a hawk all night.

B.text: Leave early. Don't tell them why.

C.text: Bring up the ex on the ride home. Casually. With detail.

D.text: Pretend not to notice. Spend the week investigating the ex on social media.

questions.text: You see them like a 2019 photo of someone you don't know on Instagram.

A.text: Check that person's entire profile. Their job. Where they live. Who they follow.

B.text: Like an old photo of one of your exes in retaliation.

C.text: Bring it up casually three days later.

D.text: Note this. Be slightly less available for a few days.

questions.text: Their phone lights up next to you. You see a notification from a name you don't recognize.

A.text: Try to read the preview.

B.text: Save the name. Google it later. Check their LinkedIn.

C.text: Don't ask. Check their socials when you get home.

D.text: Ask who it is — then second-guess yourself for asking.

questions.text: You're at brunch. Mid-meal, you see them texting under the table.

A.text: Don't say anything. Excuse yourself to the bathroom. Stay in there 10 minutes.

B.text: Ask who they're texting. Tone slightly off.

C.text: Pull out your phone too. Pretend you have plans.

D.text: Watch their face. Try to read the texts in their eye movement.

questions.text: They tease you in front of their friends in a way that stings.

A.text: Laugh along — then mention it later, alone, in a 'just so you know' way.

B.text: Tease them back, edgier than they teased you.

C.text: Get quiet for the rest of the night. Make them ask what's wrong.

D.text: Laugh the loudest. Bring it up never.

questions.text: They forgot your birthday. They remember two days late and feel awful.

A.text: 'It's fine, don't worry!' Mean it half.

B.text: Accept the apology. Bring it up in three weeks during an unrelated fight.

C.text: 'Yeah.' Don't say anything else.

D.text: Forgive them out loud. Vent to three friends in detail later.

questions.text: You finally tell them what you want from this thing. They reply: 'let's just enjoy this for now.'

A.text: 'Okay, that works for me.' — even though it doesn't.

B.text: Start emotionally pulling away. Reply slower. Get colder.

C.text: Agree, then convince yourself they'll come around in 3 weeks.

D.text: End it preemptively. Better to leave than be left.

questions.text: It's 2am. They text 'u up?'

A.text: Reply 'yeah, you?' — pretend you weren't waiting.

B.text: Wait 6 hours, then reply 'sorry just saw this'.

C.text: See it. Don't reply. Stare at the screen for 20 minutes.

D.text: Reply right away with a long flirty paragraph — way too long for 2am.
